chief_complaint: painless, slippery, firm round lump in breast
hpi_details: 24-year-old female presents with a self-discovered painless, firm, mobile lump in her right upper outer breast. She noticed it 1 month ago while showering. No skin dimpling, nipple discharge, or significant family history of breast cancer.
ideas: She thinks the lump might just be a clogged milk duct or a hormonal fluid cyst linked to her monthly cycle.
concerns: She is worried that the lump is malignant breast cancer and that she will need surgery to remove her breast.
expectations: She hopes to get an ultrasound today to confirm the lump is benign and avoid having a needle biopsy.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Breast Fibroadenoma is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management for Breast Fibroadenoma emphasizes ultrasound/mammogram with core biopsy to confirm, followed by observation, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

reference_soap.subjective:
Chief Complaint: painless, slippery, firm round lump in breast

24-year-old female presents with a self-discovered painless, firm, mobile lump in her right upper outer breast. She noticed it 1 month ago while showering. No skin dimpling, nipple discharge, or significant family history of breast cancer.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals normal. Right breast exam reveals a 2x2 cm well-circumscribed, firm, highly mobile, non-tender mass in the upper outer quadrant. No axillary lymphadenopathy. No overlying skin changes.
reference_soap.plan: Reassurance given its classic benign features in a young woman. Proceed with breast ultrasound to confirm diagnosis. Observation and clinical follow-up.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Breast Fibroadenoma
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Breast Fibroadenoma
Implement evidence-based management plan: Ultrasound/mammogram, core biopsy to confirm, observation

teaching.one_liner: A benign, hormonally-responsive breast tumor typically found in younger women — smooth, firm, mobile ('slippery'), and painless.
red_flags: A mass that becomes fixed, irregular, or rapidly enlarging — reconsider malignancy

must_ask.say: Does the lump move easily when you press on it?
Is the lump painful or tender?
When did you notice it, and has it changed in size?
Does the size seem to change with your period?
Does breast cancer run in your family?

history.answer: About a month ago, I felt a round, firm lump in my right breast while showering, so I came in to get it checked.
I first discovered it about four weeks ago while soaping myself in the shower; it seemed to appear out of nowhere.
It is just one lump in the upper outer area of my right breast, and I haven't noticed any lumps on the left.
It feels smooth and firm like a marble, and it slips and moves around very easily when I touch it.
It has stayed about the same size since I noticed it a month ago, roughly the size of a grape.
No, it doesn't change in size with my menstrual cycle, and it doesn't swell before my period.
No, there is no pain or tenderness at all, even when I press right on it.
I haven't noticed any dimpling, puckering, redness, or change in the skin, and my nipple looks completely normal.
No, there has not been any fluid, blood, or discharge coming from either nipple.
No, I felt around my armpits and didn't find any lumps or swollen spots.
No fever, chills, or feelings of warmth in my breasts.
I have never been pregnant or breastfed, and I don't have any cracks or cuts on my nipples.
No weight loss, bone pain, chronic cough, or shortness of breath; I feel healthy overall.
No, I haven't had any trauma or injury to my chest, and I've never had any breast procedures.
I have never had any breast lumps before, no prior biopsies, and no radiation to my chest.
No, I have never had a mammogram or a breast ultrasound before this visit.
My first period was when I was 13, and my cycles come regularly every 28 to 30 days. I have never been pregnant.
No, I am not taking birth control pills, hormonal treatments, or any medications that affect hormones.
I do not have any chronic medical conditions like diabetes or high blood pressure.
I have never had surgery and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I do not take any prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or vitamins.
I have no known allergies to any medications.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco products.
I only drink alcohol socially, about a glass of beer once or twice a month.
I work as an office clerk and live in an apartment with a roommate.
No one in my family has had breast cancer, ovarian cancer, or any other early cancers.
My last period started about two weeks ago and was normal.
There is no possibility of pregnancy; I am not currently sexually active.
I thought it might just be a hormonal cyst or a clogged duct that popped up with my monthly cycle.

I can't stop worrying that this might be breast cancer and that I'll end up needing surgery or losing my breast. I'm hoping to get an ultrasound today to know for sure that it's harmless and won't require a painful biopsy.

exam.finding: Patient appears comfortable, well-nourished, and in no acute physical distress.
Blood pressure is 118/76 mmHg, pulse is 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 14 breaths per minute, and body temperature is 36.7°C.

Visual inspection shows symmetric breasts without skin dimpling, erythema, or nipple retraction; palpation reveals a 2x2 cm well-circumscribed, firm, highly mobile, non-tender mass in the right upper outer quadrant, with no nipple discharge and no axillary lymphadenopathy.
No palpable cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy bilaterally.
